logic_errors.finding: Acknowledgement catches BaseException from binding and silently returns False, swallowing KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit rather than preserving nonlocal control flow. Poisoning and denial are appropriate; suppressing these origins is not documented by the public method or implementer contract.
logic_errors.contract_basis: Review requires supported public-path interrupt/failure-origin preservation. The acknowledgement docstring at line 245 describes event acknowledgement, not suppression of process exit/cancellation. The implementation report contract.poison promises denial after reached failure, while the general failure model in wiki/guides/runtime-publication-contract.md:45-51,151-152 preserves interrupts and origins; that proposal is not misapplied as schema-2 authority for this schema-1 helper.
logic_errors.actual_evidence: Nine calibrated acknowledgement cases reached actual borrowed-root fstat, owned-file fstat or fixed-entry stat: OSError, KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit all returned False and poisoned. Each had a preceding successful append/True acknowledgement and the injected origin traceback retained the reached fault frame. All six interrupt/exit combinations suppressed the origin. Separate expected-contract oracles for KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit both failed as assertions, not import failures.
logic_errors.calibration: OSError-to-False denial is treated as the intended query boundary, not a separate defect. This finding does not claim a false acknowledgement, publication or world admission.

logic_errors.finding: A reached pre-release close failure retains the owned file descriptor and cooperative writer lock without a supported recoverable ownership/status boundary. close sets _closed before attempting release, so another close silently does nothing while the lock still excludes a fresh process. Failed construction returns no journal object and leaves its allocated fd/lock live after a pre-release cleanup failure; the origin gets only a generic cleanup note.
logic_errors.contract_basis: The implementer report contract.serialization describes an owned lifetime writer fd until explicit close, and contract.cleanup says pre-release and released failures are distinguished. Existing tests at tests/test_runtime_publication_journal.py:434-462 only prove one attempt and manually close a retained descriptor in fixture code. The bounded review specifically requires distinguishing harness cleanup from production release and establishing explicit recoverability/status on supported pre-release failures. The unchanged close_owned helper is accepted: this finding does not prescribe blind close retries or changing that helper.
logic_errors.actual_evidence: Four close cases paired OSError/KeyboardInterrupt with release-before-raise versus raise-before-release. Released cases had EBADF and a fresh subprocess could open; pre-release cases retained a valid regular-file fd, _closed=True, second close made no syscall, acknowledgement denied, and an independent subprocess was still locked. Two constructor compound-fault cases preserved the original KeyboardInterrupt and sanitized cleanup note; pre-release cleanup retained one extra /proc/self/fd entry and blocked a fresh subprocess, released cleanup retained zero and reopened normally. A separate original-read-OSError plus pre-release cleanup-KeyboardInterrupt oracle also failed because the owned descriptor remained live.
logic_errors.calibration: All ownership/lock observations occurred before explicit harness-only cleanup. Harness finally blocks then released only captured synthetic descriptors, after which subprocess reopening succeeded. OSError-before-release is a labeled injection, not a claim that Linux EIO necessarily retains an fd; pre-release KeyboardInterrupt independently demonstrates the supported control-flow boundary. No stronger same-UID/privileged exclusion, automatic rollback, or guaranteed physical release after every kernel close error is asserted.

suggestions: If acknowledgement intentionally converts ordinary binding I/O errors to a poisoned False result, document that query boundary separately from propagation of nonlocal control flow.
Specify an explicit unresolved-cleanup ownership/status boundary without retrying a potentially released/reused descriptor. A one-attempt policy is not proof of cleanup completion.

Constructor os.open and initial borrowed-root fstat are outside the redaction try block. Reached injected OSError objects retain their original filename there. This is a scope note, not a security finding: the actual open accepts a fixed public basename and the report only promises generated-error redaction on append/close. Do not generalize that promise to all constructor errors.
The allowed reason enum is not coupled to the event enum. No such coupling is specified by this data-only journal contract, so accepting intent/io_failure is not classified as an error.
summary: Data-only journal persistence, strict replay, generation/phase denial and append failure handling passed scoped checks, but acknowledgement suppresses nonlocal control flow and pre-release cleanup failures strand owned writer resources; scoped approval withheld.

Strict canonical six-field UTF-8 JSONL replay refuses duplicate/unknown keys, malformed types, whitespace/CRLF, torn rows, invalid phases/generations and overlong records without truncation or repair.

Constructor open/root-fstat/file-fstat/flock/pread faults preserve reached origin object/traceback and release normally allocated writer fds; invalid decode also releases. Compound cleanup faults preserve the original error rather than masking it.

Actual one-write append faults, short write, file/root fsync, pre-read/readback, readback mismatch, and pre/post binding faults poison without retry, preserve confirmed snapshots as historical observations, and deny volatile acknowledgement.
Complete failed-append bytes reopen in a fresh process as historical only; torn short-write bytes remain unchanged and cannot reopen. No committed-looking record creates restart authority.
Exact built-in root int and record/ack string checks precede overridable subtype behavior. Existing append/close thread serialization test passes.
